items.title: 2026 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget Report
notes: Report from A. McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer

Adam McNabb, Managing Director of Corporate Services & Treasurer introduced the 2026 preliminary draft capital budget. He indicated staff is seeking direction from Council to include the 2026 Preliminary Draft Capital Budget in the overall 2026 Staff Draft Budget. He outlined the topics to discuss including the 10-year Bridge and Major Culvert Plan, the 2027 to 2035 Capital Forecast (if complete), a projection of debt requirements, a calculation of debt capacity and repayment limits, the results of the Public Engagement Survey, and any other budget related matters ready for Council’s consideration.

Adam McNabb and other members of staff spoke to the 2026 proposed capital budget through the storyboard, including the New Housing Action Plan, the Sportsplex Grounds Plan and Lands Site Development study, Active Transportation intersection improvements and

sidewalk/wayfinding and signage improvements, various bridge, road and culvert works, the Fergus water and wastewater treatment plant works, the water meter modernization, the Belwood Hall accessibility design and renovation project, the corporate operations facility, and the Sportsplex roof
Mark Bradey, Manager of Finance & Deputy Treasurer provided an overview of the 2026 draft capital budget, noting the new IP column, explaining the various funding sources and responding to questions.

Staff responded to questions regarding the ERP System, in particular the HR and Health & Safety module, the plans and studies to be completed in 2026 to re-zone the site for recreational use and develop a high-level layout for future facilities, the scope of the Cameron Street project, connecting the wayfinding signage and parking, the timing of the 29WG bridge replacement and the replacement of the watermain on Douglas Crescent project.
Gerri Atkinson, Manager of Wastewater Services provided an overview of the Fergus WWTP Aeration Basin Rehabilitation project and responded to questions regarding the Fergus WWTP headworks.

Dino Masiero, Manager of Water Services and Environmental Sustainability provided an overview of the water meter modernization project, noting the water meters were originally installed in 2003 and are at the end of their life expectancy. He indicated there are approximately 5,000 meters scheduled for replacement.

Staff continued to respond to questions regarding the water supply projects and the expected disruptions in the various neighbourhoods, the various funding allotments/opportunities for the Belwood Hall Accessibility Design and Renovation, the communication strategy to share the progress of the Corporate Operations Facility, the inclusion of a new vehicle for By-law Enforcement, the purpose of the Rugby Building Future Use Strategy, the fencing around the Elora Cemetery, and the extent of the Provost Lane and Fergus Curling Club parking lot improvements.
Mayor Watters called for a 6 minute recess, the meeting resumed at 10:40 am.

Pat Newson, Managing Director of Community Services highlighted several of the projects and equipment contained within the budget, including outdoor basketball courts at Victoria Park, the utility vehicle and trail groomer, the Webster Park upgrades and the disc golf course in Elora.

Discussions continued and staff responded to questions regarding Confederation Park improvements, relocating forestry to the operating budget, timing and public engagement for Strathallan Park redesign, new vending machines in facilities, and the status of the Bissell Park project.

11.3 Battery Energy Storage Community Benefit Contribution Agreement Report from D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, indicating the agreement is typical between BESS providers and the municipalities they are a part of. It outlines an annual contribution that the BESS provider provides to the municipality (i.e. dollar amount per Megawatt or MW of project contract capacity). Based on research conducted and discussions with other municipalities, the typical contribution amount per MW is in the range of $500 to $1,100 per MW annually.
D. Wilson responded to questions regarding a regular reporting structure, future reapportionment and discussions regarding the agreement.

items.title: Curt McQueen on behalf of Fergus Elora District Soccer and Highland
notes: Rugby appeared in support of prioritizing a multi-use recreational facility in the 2026 capital budget. He indicated the need to provide facilities currently not available in Centre Wellington, such as turf, a walking track and a gymnasium is important. He noted the ability to partner with the high school and improve the activity health and wellness of the community.

notes: prioritizing the multi use recreational facility to support the very popular sport of basketball in the community. They responded to questions regarding sports tourism, the desire to access additional facilities and the ability to host camps and tournaments.

items.title: Anthea Milliken, resident appeared before Council suggesting an option
notes: be considered to incorporate all the facilities required using the funds available. She questioned the process undertaken and the underlying assumptions that appear to be driving the high costs.

items.title: Multi Use Recreation Facility Studies
notes: Report from P. Newson, Managing Director of Community Services Tracey McQueen and Terry Allyman explained the purpose of the study and business plan is to determine whether a proposed capital construction project is practical, sustainable and aligned with community needs. They highlighted the community engagement and data collection practices as well as the amenities and users. T. Allyman noted the preferred location at the community sportsplex either as an extension or a stand-alone facility. They outlined the proposed funding formula and the community benefit, the comparable municipal facilities and rental rates, the staffing plan and the projected annual operating revenues and expenditures.
Councillor Wilton suggested a friendly amendment to paragraph 3, to add “the Economic Prosperity and Growth Advisory Committee”.

items.title: Economic Development and Tourism Strategy
notes: Report from B. Salmon, Managing Director of Planning and Development
D. Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided a background on the study and introduced Catherine Oosterbaan, Oosterbaan Strategy and Terrilyn Kunopaski, Tante Consulting Inc.

Catherine Oosterbaan, Oosterbaan Strategy and Terrilyn Kunopasky, Tante Consulting Inc., outlined the goals of the report, the approach taken, and the public consultation/engagement conducted. They outlined the strengths, opportunities, aspirations and results (SOAR) and highlighted the strategic pillars that include; capacity, economic growth & resilience, workforce & livability, destination development & visitor management, brand identify, marketing & communications, placemaking and investment readiness & infrastructure.
The consultants and staff responded to questions from Council regarding sports and Agri tourism, and the impending implementation of the Municipal Accommodation Tax.

motions.item_title: Connecting Links Grant Application - Tower and Bridge Street Repaving
motions.text: THAT the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington directs staff to submit an application under the Ontario Ministry of Transportation's Connecting Links grant program (Intake 11: 2026-2027) for repaving Tower Street and Bridge Street in Fergus; AND THAT Council delegates authority to the Chief Administrative Officer and Managing Director of Corporate Services/Treasurer to execute any funding agreements and any other documents related to securing the funding should the Township's grant application be successful; AND THAT should the grant application be successful, Council approves funding the Township's portion for the project, estimated to be $130,000, from the General Capital Reserve.

motions.item_title: Priority Setting for Indoor Recreation Facilities
motions.text: That Council direct staff to include a Multi-Use Recreation Facility in the 2026 Capital Ten-Year Plan; and further, that staff be directed to prioritize the design and development of the Multi-Use Recreation Facility at the Fergus Sportsplex, while evaluating the feasibility of integrating ice into the expansion design, in order to better position the Township to capture external funding, respond to community growth, and create a truly accessible, integrated recreation hub that blends sport with fitness, health, and inclusive community programming. Mayor Watters did not accept the “friendly amendment” put forward.
